owner_creation.analysis: OWN-08 owns saved prompt prototypes, decoded table nodes/buffers, cached environment copies and allocated message replacements. Static option descriptors only point to these different owner domains.
owner_creation.invariant: Configuration pointers must identify their owning storage class.
limitations: One configuration precedence rule does not unify allocation lifetimes.

aliases_escapes.analysis: OWN-08 lgetenv can return table bytes, cached copies or borrowed libc environment storage; pr_expand returns shared scratch text. Retaining any result requires the corresponding owner to survive updates.
aliases_escapes.invariant: Borrowed lookup and expansion results must not become independent owners.
limitations: A later prompt expansion overwrites the same message scratch array.

callback_targets.analysis: OWN-08 option scanning invokes the typed ofunc from its selected loption and then frees temporary str. The static table binds the buffer option to opt_b with the same C signature.
callback_targets.invariant: Option callbacks must copy any parameter they retain.
limitations: Typing the callback does not establish its shared-state exclusion contract.

invalidation.analysis: OWN-08 prompt replacement frees the selected prototype before saving new text; message initialization explicitly invalidates previously borrowed help pointers. Replacement ordering is not uniformly copy-before-free.
invalidation.invariant: No consumer may retain an invalidated prototype or message alias.
limitations: M0-MEM-001 covers these raw lifetime contracts without a new failure claim.

mutation_commit.analysis: OWN-08 lesskey_text publishes command/edit buffers directly, copies variable expansion into a distinct owner, then deinitializes parser variable bytes. That current transfer repairs the historical M0-LEAK-003 mechanism.
mutation_commit.invariant: Published table bytes must outlive the staging parser descriptor.
limitations: The existing finding remains open for maintained independent disposition.

release_pair.analysis: OWN-08 release_cmd_table frees only owns_buffer data before the node; prompt saved-option replacement copies before free. Message replacement uses ownership flags to avoid freeing borrowed defaults.
release_pair.invariant: Borrowed defaults must not take owned-allocation release paths.
limitations: Current release repairs do not close M0-LEAK-005 or M0-LEAK-006.

error_cleanup.analysis: OWN-08 failed parsing deinitializes all three staged buffers before returning, and evar expansion frees copied lookup values and replacement nodes on normal completion. Fatal allocation still lacks a general RAII transaction.
error_cleanup.invariant: Parse failure must not free data retained by an older table.
limitations: Normal-return cleanup is not a proof for every fatal allocation boundary.

signals_handoff.analysis: OWN-08 remains reachable from sigusr environment lookup and queue creation. lgetenv can allocate cache nodes, so source-correct parsing and precedence do not make configuration access signal-safe (M0-SIG-002).
signals_handoff.invariant: Handler dispatch must defer lookup and allocation to ordinary execution.
limitations: No configuration-source changes or runtime campaigns are performed here.

src/signal.rs.relationship: sigusr at src/signal.rs:86-100 calls lgetenv before ungetsc; that invokes the shared configuration lookup/cache path covered by OWN-08 from an asynchronous handler.
